name: A year of books of a Brunei Darussalam trading and consulting company that files no periodic return on sales

documents.why: A domestic sale of services, BN-S-NA: the not-subject code posts the line's base and nothing else — no tax line, no declaration box.
A domestic sale of goods, BN-S-NA on the goods side too: the code draws no distinction the way a real turnover tax would between what is sold.

An export of goods to a customer outside Brunei Darussalam: BN-S-NA applies exactly as it does to V2's domestic sale, because there is no turnover tax to zero-rate. The one percent tax on approved exports (Income Tax Act, section 8A) is an income tax assessed on the exporter's gross proceeds, not a charge on this invoice, so it posts nothing here.
A credit note against V2, a partial return of goods — the golden's sale-side credit note.
A second domestic service sale, to spread the scenario across more than one month and leave an invoice a part-payment settles only partly.
A third domestic goods sale, settled by nothing in this scenario — an open receivable the trial balance has to carry at the year end.
A domestic purchase of trading inventory, BN-P-NA: the purchase side of the not-subject code, posting the base and nothing to recover.
A recurring domestic expense, office rent, paid in full by E3 — the golden's matched payment on the purchase side.

An import of components from a supplier outside Brunei Darussalam: BN-P-NA posts the base and nothing else. Customs import duty, where the goods are dutiable, is a duty on specified goods paid at the border and is not modelled; the goods in this scenario are taken as not dutiable.
A credit note against P1, a partial return of defective stock — the golden's purchase-side credit note, beside CN1 on the sale side.

A purchase of a fixed asset, computer equipment, booked straight to the balance sheet rather than to an expense account — proof BN-P-NA posts its base wherever the document line's own account sends it, and nowhere of its own choosing.
A recurring administrative purchase booked to the retirement fund contributions account: a service fee for administering the employee retirement fund contributions, posting its base and nothing else.
A recurring administrative purchase, accounting and company secretarial fees — the audited accounts a company files with its income tax return depend on one.

payments.why: An inbound payment that exactly settles V1 — the golden's matched payment on the sale side.
An inbound part-payment on account, matched to nothing — the golden's unmatched payment and the open item a return computed from matchings has to survive.
An outbound payment that exactly settles P2 — the matched payment on the purchase side.
An outbound part-payment on account to a supplier, matched to nothing — the unmatched payment on the purchase side.
